answer: Yes. As of the CDC page updated September 12, 2026, everyone 6 months and older is recommended to get a flu vaccine every season, with rare exceptions [1]. Vaccination is especially important for people at higher risk of serious complications, including adults 65 and older [1]. WHO likewise says annual vaccination is the most effective way to prevent influenza and recommends it for older adults, pregnant women, health workers, and people with chronic medical conditions [2]. Whether and when to get vaccinated is a personal medical decision, so it's best to talk with a clinician about your situation.

notes.focus: Whether adults should get the seasonal flu vaccine this season, according to current health authority guidance.

keyPoints.text: CDC recommends that everyone 6 months of age and older get a flu vaccine every season, with rare exceptions.
CDC says vaccination is especially important for people at higher risk of serious complications, including adults 65 and older.
WHO states annual vaccination is the most effective way to prevent influenza.
WHO recommends annual vaccination for older adults, pregnant women, health workers and people with chronic medical conditions.

mayBeStale.text: The WHO fact sheet is dated 2026-08-20, so it may predate later seasonal updates.
